title: Frontend CI, portable release verification, and ESM scanner hardening
reason: The maintained frontend now uses feature-local .mjs helpers, CI and generic scanners do not yet explicitly require UI tests, moderate-or-stricter audit severity, or complete ESM helper coverage, and verify:release directly invokes bare mvn instead of honoring the configured runtime-policy executable path.
oldRule: CI accepts a high-only frontend audit and infers UI tests from build behavior; verify:release directly invokes bare mvn and bypasses the configured Maven executable; several generic governance scanners omit executable .mjs helpers and route discovery is the accidental mechanism that keeps helpers out of the UI graph.
newRule: CI and verify:release explicitly run the UI test suite and accept only a single literal info, low, or moderate audit threshold with development dependencies included. CI merges workflow, container, job, and step environments before accepting the exact Maven reactor; it recursively expands declared YAML environment aliases and normalizes frontend audit working directories, npm launch wrappers, executable expressions, subcommands, arguments, and prefix paths without conflating known repository-root audits. Unresolved dynamic npm programs that may target the frontend fail closed. Local release verification resolves Maven from runtime policy with a standard-command fallback and preserves fail-fast command semantics. Non-route code scanners include .mjs; route discovery remains explicitly limited to real Vue/page extensions.
regressionContract: Require a dedicated unconditional ruoyi-ui test step in CI.

Accept only one literal info, low, or moderate audit level with development dependencies included; reject high, critical, missing, dynamic, duplicated, conflicting, fix, production-only, or omitted-dependency forms.
Treat every frontend audit or test attempt as required verification for failure-mask and unsafe-control analysis, even when its arguments are invalid.
Merge workflow, container, job, and step environments before accepting Maven coverage; reject MAVEN_ARGS and dynamic or test-weakening Maven/JVM option variables.
Reject persistent GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH mutation before fixed verification commands.

Recursively expand declared YAML environment aliases and simple run-block assignments; normalize literal and known-root frontend working directories, cd/pushd options, npm and process wrappers, shell and Actions executable expressions, dynamic npm subcommands and arguments, environment-resolved commands, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, and prefix paths; fail closed on unresolved dynamic frontend audit programs while independent repository-root audits do not count toward frontend uniqueness.
Make finalize:change append one well-separated changelog entry per exact change id and remain idempotent when rerun without a summary.
Resolve release-verification Maven through the configured runtime-policy path with a standard mvn fallback, execute the exact integration reactor once, and stop at the first failed release step.
Include .mjs in code, ownership, dependency, permission, boundary, lifecycle, reference, deletion, duplicate, and text-hygiene scanning.
Keep .mjs helpers out of generated frontend route/page records.
Keep plain .mjs helpers visible to ownership scanning without registering them as components.
Run real UI tests, a moderate audit, production build, release verification, and the complete repository gate.
checklist: Explain old rule and new rule.
List sample files proving the project base needs this rule.
Run npm run check after the rule proposal is accepted.
verification: Final focused governance and scanner regressions pass 234/234, including 42/42 CI-hardening tests; portable release-verifier and anti-false-green coverage passes 94/94.
Final verify:release passes with 480/480 Node tests and 60/60 Java tests including both MySQL/Testcontainers integration tests.
UI tests pass 7/7, the moderate full dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities across 360 dependencies, and the production build transforms 2601 modules.
